# Domainry Builder V1

Drive every development batch through:

```text
requirements → domain facts → calculation ownership/persistence/correction → capability discovery → model → apply → verify → done
```

Platform capabilities determine the implementation mapping; they never determine the business facts. Do not start from Dataset, Report, metadata, an Action shape, or any other Runtime feature and work backward into a domain model.

The frontend under `frontend/**` is evidence of product demand, not automatically a complete business specification. Inspect its routes, screens, typed API contract, Mock adapters, tests, roles, states, and copy read-only while settling requirements and domain truth; never promote Mock behavior into business truth. Later integration work follows the explicit frontend mutation boundary below: route each mismatch to the owner proved by current contracts and real behavior instead of forcing it into the backend; frontend-owned mismatches become findings, never edits.

Read [development-guide.md](references/development-guide.md) completely before starting a whole-project batch. Use it as the only execution workflow.

## Semantic execution invariants

Before model authoring, bind every acceptance journey in the existing PRD/TODO to its requirement, actor, formal Runtime session/principal source, Runtime-derived context and canonical identifiers, isolated setup records, command and read surface, non-empty positive oracle, exact denied/conflict oracle, durable effect, and dependent journeys. Do not create a second plan. `project acceptance prepare` must compile these bindings into the denominator's required `domainry-semantic-acceptance-contract-v1`; an unmapped case, actor/role mismatch, unbound command/fact, shared setup, or divergent oracle is a preparation failure, not a harness TODO. Treat Runtime-owned IDs, hierarchy values, principal claims, and other canonical representations as opaque: resolve them through `GET /identity/principal-context`, the published typed client, formal seed/admin path, or persisted Runtime result and carry the returned value unchanged. Never construct, trim, pad, normalize, inject, or query Runtime-owned persistence to discover them; if no formal source exists, keep the affected journey blocked.

Every scope-sensitive journey requires a same-record contrast through real Runtime sessions: the matching actor must observe the targeted non-empty result, a non-matching actor must receive the contractually exact concealment/denial, and a broader actor must observe the record when such a role is part of the requirement. Empty collections, null results, zero aggregates, or an arbitrary HTTP error never prove success unless that exact outcome is the confirmed requirement. Denied/conflict probes also prove unchanged durable state. Use fresh per-scenario identifiers so one case cannot pass from another case's residue.

After the current source is finalized and focused tests pass, run one highest-risk semantic canary across formal identity/context resolution → command → persisted effect → actor-visible read-back before the broad Runtime integration round. A canary failure blocks dependent journeys: capture the complete root-cause fan-out, repair it once at its owner, and rerun only the invalidated checks. The canary is execution order, not permission to publish a partial model or reduce the frozen acceptance denominator.

## Loaded Skill and CLI identity

Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact filesystem path of the `SKILL.md` loaded for this task. Run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"` once at task start. Set `DOMAINRY_CLI` to its returned `cli`, which must equal the current package's single executable `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-cli"` (`domainry-cli.exe` on Windows), and use its `session_id`, `todo`, compact `resume_packet`, and one-time `authoring_context` for the whole task. The context bundle contains the canonical discovery/schema command sequence, project model inventory, routed reference paths, and small generic decision examples; use it after context compaction instead of repeating broad repository or capability discovery. Re-run the resolver only if the project root or Host session identity changes. This one CLI exposes only the model, capability discovery, Action/Connector implementation, verification, packaging, and Runtime commands listed below. Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" version --json` before any other Builder command. Use `"$DOMAINRY_CLI"` for every command shown by this Skill and its references; never discover a CLI through `PATH` or substitute another Skill's binary.

## Canonical normal-development CLI map

Use only the applicable commands below, in TODO order. These are the complete normal project-development command families; do not invent a neighboring command name. Add one pinned `--environment <name>` or `--service <url>` target wherever shown and keep it consistent once selected. Use a command's `--help` for flags when a placeholder needs resolution.

```text
# initialization
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" version --json

# SDK bootstrap when the delivered Runtime Client package or disclosure contract is absent
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project materialize runtime-client --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" [target]

# platform capability reuse discovery before modeling
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" contract capability-categories --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" contract capability-category --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --key <fixed-category-key>

# backend modeling: edit backend/model/*.json, then inspect the pending plan
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model validate --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"

# bootstrap model files once for a project created before the model workflow
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model export --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"

# release: the single release command (full semantics: references/backend-model.md)
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model apply --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path <domain-qualified-module> --product-surfaces <business_workspace|consumer_portal|business_workspace,consumer_portal> [target] [--allow-destructive]
# existing Builder delivery only: rerun with the CLI-emitted evolution audit SHA-256 and review reason
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model apply --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path <domain-qualified-module> --product-surfaces <same-reviewed-surfaces> [target] --evolution-audit-sha256 <emitted-sha256> --evolution-reason <reviewed-reason>

# approved source gaps only
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project source prepare --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" action context --projection coding --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" [--evolution-audit-sha256 <sha256>] <object.action>
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" action scaffold apply --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" [--evolution-audit-sha256 <sha256>] ... <object.action>
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" action source apply --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" [--evolution-audit-sha256 <sha256>] ... --input - <object.action>
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" connector definition --json [target] <connector>
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" connector context --projection coding --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" <connector.provider>
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" connector scaffold apply --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" ... <connector.provider>

# static source-contract gate: run after writing or changing any handler/domain source and
# require exit 0 BEFORE every source finalize — same analyzer finalize enforces, so discarded
# call results/errors and forbidden raw metadata keys surface locally instead of as a
# finalize rejection round
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project check --json --scope actions --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"

# re-finalize after implementing approved source gaps, before the first backend compile or test
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project source finalize --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"

# verification and managed Runtime
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project verify --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project package --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" runtime-process start --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --bundle <current-project-relative-bundle> --address 127.0.0.1:<dedicated-port>
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" runtime-process status --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
# freeze the acceptance denominator, run the platform runner first, then check results
# (runner-first rule and exact-set contract: references/verification.md)
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance prepare --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance run --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --cases standard --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json
# after a model evolution only: re-record ONLY the reported stale/missing cases (incremental flow: references/verification.md)
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance stale-report --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance check --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" runtime-process stop --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

`model apply` is the only release command in this flow; its complete convergence, checklist, destructive-consent (`--allow-destructive`, rename = delete + create), and evolution-audit (`evolution_review_required` → rerun with the emitted SHA-256 and review reason) semantics live in [backend-model.md](references/backend-model.md). Always pass the reviewed `--product-surfaces`: it is the backend-to-frontend integration boundary used by materialization, not authorization to generate or redesign page source, and backend materialization inside apply must never create, modify, or delete `frontend/**`. After a failure, repair the model files or reported input and rerun the same command; never invent a neighboring release command.

## Session TODO

Maintain exactly one development document for the current Agent session:

```text
<project>/.domainry/development/<agent-session-id>.md
```

Use the real session/thread ID returned by the context resolver. Its primary sources are `DOMAINRY_AGENT_SESSION_ID` in Domainry, `CODEX_THREAD_ID` in Codex, or an equivalent explicit Host value; its temporary Domainry fallback is the unique active log session whose `cwd` equals the exact project root. Treat the ID as an opaque safe filename segment. Never generate a replacement UUID, select the globally newest log session, accept an ambiguous project match, guess, shorten, or reuse another session's ID.

At session start:

1. Resolve the current host-provided Agent session ID.
2. Resume `.domainry/development/<agent-session-id>.md` when the same session already created it.
3. Otherwise create that file from [DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md](assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md).
4. Record the exact session ID, batch goal, original requirement, project mode, execution scope, frontend mutation scope, and concrete tasks.
5. Run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-gates.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" sync` once. Execute the TODO strictly top-to-bottom per the template's execution rules; never check later work merely because it happened out of order.
6. Close checkboxes through the evidence Gate's `run`, `attach`, or explicit `mark --status not_applicable` commands, not by writing success prose. Bind command receipts or non-empty project-local evidence artifacts to the applicable source, model/Blueprint, and Runtime identities. Before leaving a stage, run its `status --stage <stage> --require-complete`; changed evidence content or bound identity becomes stale and blocks completion.
7. At completion, require Gate status for `verify` and `done`, close every finding, set `Current stage: done`, and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-todo-check.py" --todo "$TODO_PATH"` once immediately before the final response; repair any reported inconsistency and rerun until it passes.

One session owns only its own TODO and must not overwrite or update another session's document. A new session creates a new file even when it continues related project work; it may reference previous session documents as read-only handoff context.

Do not keep a second execution plan. Append validation findings to the current session document, finish the round, batch repairs, and revalidate until the finding inventory is empty. One artifact may support several items, but every Gate must bind the artifact and state the exact fact it proves; if later work changes the bound source, model/Blueprint, Runtime manifest, or artifact content, the Gate is stale — rerun or regenerate the evidence. The TODO checker remains only a lightweight consistency linter; the evidence Gate controls step closure, while the verification evidence ladder controls how high the final claim may reach.

If the template's physical order contradicts the real dependency order, fix and validate `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md` before using or releasing that Skill version — never compensate by executing items out of order.

## Project boundary

Keep the project canonical:

```text
backend/model/*.json  Agent-authored backend metadata inventory
backend/reports/*.sql  Project-owned Report SQL referenced by model `sql_file`; model apply normalizes, hashes, and embeds it
backend/   project-owned Go source plus generated platform source
.domainry/development/<agent-session-id>.md  current session development TODO
.domainry/  CLI-managed delivery, contracts, receipts, artifacts, Runtime, and evidence
```

Git owns project-source development. Normal editors, file patches, formatters, dependency tools, and Git worktrees may modify project-owned source.

`frontend/**` remains read-only for requirements/domain extraction in every scope and throughout the entire task under every recorded `Frontend mutation scope`: this Skill never creates, modifies, or deletes a `frontend/**` path — the scope records the authorization context only.

`.domainry/development/*.md` is the project-owned coordination-file exception under `.domainry/`; every file is owned by the matching Agent session. Every other `.domainry/` path keeps its existing CLI/platform ownership.

Never hand-edit:

- generated source;
- frozen Project Contracts;
- Runtime manifests;
- materialization, finalization, verification, or package receipts;
- audits, caches, journals, managed Runtime state, or other CLI-owned delivery state.

Do not create symlinks, traversal paths, special files, placeholders, empty success handlers, or business source that never uses its generated capability set.

### Frontend mutation boundary

Record exactly one `Frontend mutation scope` in the TODO header:

- `integration_authorized`: the user requests a build, fix-all repair, integration, or end-to-end acceptance without narrowing the work to backend-only, and repository evidence confirms `frontend/**` is project-owned.
- `backend_only`: the user explicitly limits the task to backend work.
- `externally_owned`: the frontend is delivered by an external tool or owner that this task must not write.
- `unauthorized`: no current request authorizes frontend mutation.

The scope records the authorization boundary only; it never changes what this Skill edits. During integration, compare the explicit requirement, typed frontend API, published Runtime contract, Mock/tests, and real Runtime response before assigning a defect. Repair a backend or Runtime gap at its owner; never hide it behind a frontend compatibility adapter, fabricated fallback, or altered Mock. When evidence assigns a defect to `frontend/**` or a Mock, record it as a finding — owner `frontend`, minimal reproduction, contract basis — in every scope, including `integration_authorized`; never edit `frontend/**`. A frontend-owned defect that truly blocks a backend journey makes that journey explicitly blocked; do not mislabel the defect as a platform owner gap.

End-to-end acceptance in this Skill is backend end-to-end: real managed-Runtime HTTP/SSE/worker/database behavior, bound to the same TODO and evidence Gate source identity ([verification.md](references/verification.md)). Browser-layer UI verification is outside this Skill's acceptance scope.

## Initialization

Identity binding through the context resolver and `version --json` is setup, not a workflow stage or TODO gate (see Loaded Skill and CLI identity above). The packaged CLI has no update, sync, doctor, audit, repair, rollback, or migration command surface.

Every V2 project command uses `.domainry/builder/**` as its only managed Builder state root; legacy-root migration semantics are in [development-guide.md](references/development-guide.md) (Initialization) — never move, merge, or recreate a managed root by hand.

For a new project, verify the project root itself is one initialized Git worktree before any project-mutating CLI command (exact procedure in the guide); never initialize an existing project without authorization or create a nested repository inside another worktree.

## requirements

Before metadata modeling, inspect the delivered frontend read-only and convert it into a backend dependency contract. For a new project or a complete Mock-to-Runtime replacement, create or update `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` from [BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md](assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md). For a light existing-project increment, record a traceable PRD delta in the current session TODO or update the existing backend PRD; do not manufacture a second full document when the accepted baseline remains valid.

When the input requirement document is already structured, author the PRD in **reference mode** (rules in the guide): cite source sections instead of restating them and write only supplements — a supplement layer typically under one third of the source size, with the critical-ambiguity table and traceability unrelaxed.

Record `Execution scope: requirements_only` when the user asks only for analysis, requirements, or domain design and says not to develop. In that scope, stop after the requirements and domain-truth Gates, omit model/apply/implementation/Runtime/verify sections, and close `done` only as a requirements artifact result; do not claim delivery, integration, or any L1-L5 implementation evidence. Every build, repair, integration, or acceptance request uses `Execution scope: implementation` and continues through the full applicable workflow.

Use the evidence precedence order and the `confirmed`/`recommended`/`open`/`frontend_only`/`legacy_reference` classification defined in [development-guide.md](references/development-guide.md); preserve conflicts instead of silently selecting the most convenient source, and keep concrete file/route evidence.

Extract the complete requirement inventory (routes/journeys, actors/roles, objects/fields, queries, commands, states, calculations, authorization/scope, errors, transactions/idempotency, schedules/connectors, external effects, frontend-only presentation — full checklist in the guide) and build the trace `frontend evidence → requirement ID → Runtime owner → metadata/source implementation → permission/scope → acceptance journey`. A visual affordance is evidence of intent, not proof of its business rule.

Do not infer critical rules: an unresolved critical ambiguity (the guide's Resolve critical ambiguity list) blocks domain-truth design and all affected downstream modeling. Non-critical open items may proceed only when their assumption, owner, fallback, and excluded acceptance scope are explicit.

## domain truth design

Before materializing the SDK, discovering capabilities, or authoring metadata, read [domain-truth-and-settlement.md](references/domain-truth-and-settlement.md) completely and close the domain-truth Gate: distinguish occurred facts, summaries, and simulations, and close every calculation's ownership/persistence/correction decisions per that document. Historical financial facts must never read current Settings to recompute.

When a business event locks money, commission, points, inventory cost, or payroll input, require an atomic source-owned settlement Action with immutable snapshots and ledger entries per that document; corrections append, never mutate. Do not proceed to capability discovery while any affected ownership, persistence, or correction decision is open.

### Mandatory list Report and export Gate

Do not discover or select a Report capability until all three contracts close:

1. **List Report pagination:** every Report returning rows has bounded server pagination: platform standard or `page_size` + opaque `cursor`, maximum page size, stable ordering with a unique cursor tie-breaker, and explicit `truncated`/`total` semantics. Unbounded results, fetch-all, and browser-memory pagination are prohibited.
2. **Same-Report threshold routing:** prepare executes one bounded probe of the same Report under normalized parameters and current authorization/data Scope. The fixed threshold is 1000: an exhausted probe of `0..1000` rows yields the exact total and one synchronous governed CSV; observing row 1001 routes immediately to the platform asynchronous paged export-job substrate, whose terminal result records the final exact total. Both branches use the identical Report/SQL/source hash/parameters/Scope; a count-only or export-only second query is prohibited.
3. **Asynchronous reauthorization and terminal notification:** the `>1000` worker reconstructs the current persisted project user-role principal in the frozen workspace and compares the canonical authorization Scope before page one, failing closed on real drift; it never substitutes a manifest-only role or synthetic Surface. Only this branch publishes requester-only `completed`/`failed` Inbox notifications linked through the export job to audit and artifact.
4. **Atomic fingerprint replay:** the server canonicalizes Report key, normalized parameters, SQL/source hash, requester/workspace, authorization/data-Scope hash, format, and result version; equivalent requests atomically reuse an accepted/running job or a completed unexpired artifact (no second file, download record, or terminal notification), `audit_id` stays out of the fingerprint, and only failed/cancelled work or expired/corrupt artifacts may create one new execution through database compare-and-create. Full replay semantics: [reports.md](references/capabilities/reports.md).

Treat each line as a blocking design and acceptance Gate, not optional guidance. A published route or paginated response shape does not prove execution-level boundedness: require `pagination_trace` and `query_profile` evidence (captured on the SQLite acceptance database via `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` — never provision another database engine for profiling) and a signed cursor strategy per [reports.md](references/capabilities/reports.md); read that document whenever a page or API returns Report rows or offers Report export. If the active delivery cannot produce that proof, Report list/export scope is `acceptance_failed` with a Runtime Report owner gap — do not invent project infrastructure, exclude an in-scope requirement, or claim support.

Before capability selection or model authoring, read [production-technical-gates.md](references/production-technical-gates.md) completely and derive the current model's G01-G32 applicability matrix. This is an early prevention Gate: transaction, exact-value, authorization/RLS, paging/index, timeout/capacity, async/provider, SSE/Agent, observability, recovery, migration and evidence requirements must shape the model before publication instead of appearing for the first time in final acceptance.

## model

Derive one global resource-demand pool from the accepted backend dependency PRD and its frontend evidence. Reconcile canonical Objects, fields, Relations, Actions, Roles, permissions, data scopes, Workflows, state machines, Reports, Schedulers, Automations, Connectors, Agent Skills/Agents/Tasks/Entrypoints/Service Principals, Identity menu entries, and role-menu assignments. Assign every canonical resource one owner module and resolve conflicts before authoring the backend model files. Before the first publication, also model the new-project acceptance prerequisites — non-human acceptance identities, Workforce/departments, minimum journey seed records (see the guide) — never deferring them to final verify or seeding online credentials. Business menu definitions and role-menu assignments are not Blueprint model collections: plan them as a post-apply configuration step through the foundation Identity menu boundary (see [backend-model.md](references/backend-model.md)).

For an existing project, first understand current requirements, source, interfaces, metadata, tests, and delivery state. Plan the requested increment and its regression closure without rewriting valid existing work.

After the domain-truth Gate closes, use existing metadata capabilities first:

- Runtime CRUD and standard record operations;
- state machine and Workflow;
- Scheduler and Automation;
- record views and Reports;
- Agent Skill/Agent/Task/Entrypoint metadata and Workflow `agent_task` nodes when model reasoning is required;
- published Connector operations.

Create project-owned Handler or Connector source only for a concrete capability gap that metadata cannot express.

Before capability discovery, ensure the delivery-owned Runtime Client SDK exists. If `.domainry/builder/runtime-client-sdk/packages/runtime-client` or its capability disclosure is absent or invalid, run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project materialize runtime-client --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"` with the same pinned target used for the batch. A fetch, signature, cache, receipt, or package failure is a delivery blocker; never fabricate or bypass the SDK ([runtime-client.md](references/runtime-client.md)).

Before declaring a capability gap, check whether the required operation already exists as published platform capability: load the fixed category index once, then each selected category exactly once, using the two `contract capability-*` commands from the canonical command map. Choose only keys returned by the index; map every required operation to a returned endpoint or record the exact owner gap. An `operations_only` result proves the capability exists but is isolated from Business Workspace — it is not a missing backend capability. Admin frontend location is not backend ownership or authorization; never use `contract search` to discover Admin capability. Full discovery and reconciliation rules: [runtime-client.md](references/runtime-client.md).

Before authoring metadata, read [capabilities/README.md](references/capabilities/README.md), select the matching task profile, and load only its routed business capability documents. Read [ownership-and-extensions.md](references/ownership-and-extensions.md), [backend-model.md](references/backend-model.md), and [authorization.md](references/authorization.md) when their subject is in scope.

Use `action context`, `connector definition`, and `connector context` from the canonical command map for exact implementation contracts. V2 exposes no generic contract search command.

## apply

Author the complete backend metadata as declarative model files under `backend/model/*.json`, grouped by owning module — typically one file per module; read [backend-model.md](references/backend-model.md) for the exact file contract. Declare every module's complete inventory (Objects, Relations, Actions, Roles, authorization, data scopes, Workflows, state machines, Reports, Schedulers, Automations, Connectors, menus, seeds, acceptance) in the files before the first `model validate`: partial-resource or intermediate-file validation is a guaranteed-invalid checkpoint and is prohibited. Before that first validation, close the cross-resource preflight and its strict nested-shape card in [backend-model.md](references/backend-model.md): exact Identity menu/role-menu fields, `min`/`max` field validation keys, array-valued report metrics, the exact Report emission/`object_sql_v1` card (`value.key`, alias-only join cardinalities, and bounded SQL), closed export-control fields, and bidirectional behavior/resource ownership. Then repair the complete diagnostic batch before revalidating instead of probing one resource family at a time. After validation first reaches `state:"valid"`, freeze the model draft: do not add speculative resources or enrich identity/bootstrap metadata while recording evidence. A requirement-backed model change starts a new atomic draft and requires `model validate` plus `model plan` again. Use `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan` to inspect the pending create/update/delete/unchanged classification against the current Ledger without writing anything, and never use `apply` as a schema probe. For an existing project created before this workflow, bootstrap once with `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model export`.

Release once with `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model apply --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path <domain-qualified-module> --product-surfaces <reviewed-surfaces>`, adding one pinned explicit `--environment` or `--service` target. After a stage failure the fix is repairing the model files and re-running the same command; the full convergence, checklist, destructive-consent, and evolution-audit semantics are in [backend-model.md](references/backend-model.md). The surface value is required up front so a backend-only batch still binds its Runtime/SDK integration target before publication; it does not authorize frontend page mutation.

Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project source prepare --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"` once after materialization and before implementing approved Action gaps. It creates only missing canonical project-owned Handler/test skeletons and never overwrites existing project source; the skeletons fail closed with `*.not_implemented`, so they are an implementation inventory, not completed business behavior.

Implement approved source gaps by module, then run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project source finalize` again before the first backend compile or test; re-finalize whenever Action, Connector, domain, or other composition input changes, and only a current finalization receipt permits backend format, lint, vet, focused tests, or full tests. Failure receipts are complete `passed`/`failed`/`skipped_dependency` inventories ([verification.md](references/verification.md)); repair the complete receipt inventory as one batch. After focused tests, pass the semantic canary defined above, then execute one complete Runtime integration round: validate real API binding, authorization, persistence, idempotency, and reconciliation against the managed Runtime, route each mismatch to its actual backend, Runtime, or frontend owner under the recorded mutation scope, and collect the full finding inventory before repair, repeating until it is empty.

After implementation and real Runtime/database data acceptance, run the authorization and navigation acceptance before closing this stage: build the delta-scoped Action authorization matrix and the role effective-menu matrix against real Runtime sessions and the persisted database, exactly as specified in [development-guide.md](references/development-guide.md) (Accept authorization and navigation against real data). Never ask the user to log in, switch roles, or provide credentials — use project-provisioned non-human acceptance identities, or record the exact environment/Foundation blocker. A light batch with no Action, role, permission, scope, or menu change omits this acceptance per the template rules. Blueprint declarations or source inspection alone cannot satisfy it.

## verify

After the backend converges, read [evidence-levels.md](references/evidence-levels.md) and [verification.md](references/verification.md) completely and re-read [production-technical-gates.md](references/production-technical-gates.md), then run the final verification. Apply the complete G01-G32 denominator derived before modeling; user examples never reduce it. `project verify` and packaging establish only L1 `delivery_verified` structural/release closure, never L3 `scenario_verified` real-data behavior; project verification, packaging, and Runtime launch are internal checks inside this stage, not additional stages or start locks. Run the complete check-and-evidence inventory specified in [verification.md](references/verification.md).

After the matching managed Runtime is running and healthy, run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance prepare --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"`, execute the mechanical case families FIRST with `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance run --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --cases standard --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json`, and inspect the exact-set v2 results rows. Build business harness (assertions on `assets/acceptance-harness-core.py` only) solely for `state:"not_passed"` rows with `disposition:"needs_business_harness"`; repair `blocked_dependency`, `blocked_platform`, `unsupported_runner`, `setup_failed`, `evidence_rejected`, or `runtime_failed` at their named owner before rerunning. Then run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance check --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json`. Every assertion obtains its session through `harness.session_for_case(case)`, uses `ScenarioGraph` for isolated setup/dependencies, and applies `ReasonOracle` for the declared status/error/state/audit/positive-control reason; it never chooses a user from a role name, creates profile headers, or reads an internal identity table. The denominator is CLI-owned and never hand-edited; the exact-set contract, artifact kinds, and rejection rules are in [verification.md](references/verification.md). # Project development guide

Drive every development batch with one visible project document:

```text
<project>/.domainry/development/<agent-session-id>.md
```

The complete frontend under `frontend/**` provides concrete demand evidence through routes, screens, typed APIs, Mock adapters, tests, states, and copy. It may omit business rules or encode provisional assumptions, so inspect it read-only while extracting requirements and domain truth. Domainry Plane exposes backend capability contracts plus the transport-only `@domainry/runtime-client` the frontend consumes; Runtime machine contracts remain authoritative for data, authorization, navigation, and operation semantics. Frontend source stays read-only throughout the task; the recorded scope and evidence-based defect routing below turn frontend-owned defects into findings, never edits. See [runtime-client.md](runtime-client.md) for the client contract the frontend binds against.

The fixed stage order is the one defined in SKILL.md: requirements → domain facts → calculation ownership/persistence/correction → capability discovery → model → apply → verify → done.

## Batch scale

First record `Execution scope: requirements_only` or `implementation`. Use `requirements_only` only when the user requests analysis, requirements, or domain design and explicitly excludes development. It keeps the header, requirements, domain-truth design, and done sections; omit model, apply, Runtime, and verify sections with that reason in the header. Its `done` proves only the accepted requirements/domain artifact and must report no delivery or L1-L5 implementation claim. Any build, repair, integration, or end-to-end request is `implementation` and follows the normal full/light rules below.

Classify every batch as `full` or `light` and record the classification with its justification in the TODO header. A light batch is an existing-project increment with no new Object, Action, role, permission, scope, or menu change; everything else is a full batch. In a light batch, instantiate the TODO with only the sections the batch touches: always keep the header, the execution rules, and the `verify` and `done` stages; under `model` and `apply`, copy only the touched subsections and record every omitted subsection in the header `Sections omitted` field with what the batch does not change and the prior accepted evidence reference. When the batch changes no Action, role, permission, scope, or menu, the entire authorization and navigation acceptance section is omitted this way. Inside a copied section, a checkbox whose subject the batch does not touch may still be closed as not applicable with the same scope evidence; a subject the batch touches is never omitted or closed as not applicable. If work discovered mid-batch breaks any light criterion, reclassify the batch as full in the TODO and complete the full-track items before proceeding. A full batch follows every stage without merging.

At the start of an Agent session:

1. Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from the exact loaded `SKILL.md` path and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-context.py" --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"` once.
2. Bind `DOMAINRY_CLI`, the Agent session/thread ID, and the TODO path to the resolver's returned `cli`, `session_id`, and `todo`; retain its machine-readable `authoring_context` and compact `resume_packet` across context compaction instead of repeating broad capability/schema/reference discovery. Require that CLI to be the package's single `domainry-cli` binary and verify it with `version --json`.
3. Resolve the Agent session ID exactly as specified in SKILL.md (Session TODO); never generate, guess, shorten, or borrow an ID.
4. If `.domainry/development/<agent-session-id>.md` already exists, resume it because it belongs to the same session.
5. Otherwise create that exact file from `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md`.
6. Record the exact session ID, batch goal, original requirement, project mode, execution scope, scope, one `Frontend mutation scope`, and `requirements` as the initial current stage before implementation.
7. Add concrete project tasks beneath the template items. Do not keep a second execution plan.
8. Execute the TODO strictly top-to-bottom per the template's execution rules; check an item only in the same edit that replaces its immediately following `Evidence: pending` line with concrete evidence for that item.
9. At completion, close every item and finding, set `Current stage: done`, and run `"$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-todo-check.py" --todo "$TODO_PATH"` once immediately before the final response. Repair every reported inconsistency and rerun the checker until it passes.

One Agent session corresponds to one TODO document; never edit another session's document (ownership rules in SKILL.md, Session TODO).

The TODO is the only progress ledger and is maintained directly by the Agent; the per-checkbox `Evidence:` rules live in the template header. Keep evidence concise and link to large artifacts instead of pasting logs; if evidence becomes invalid, reopen the item. The lightweight TODO checker only detects unchecked items, pending/missing adjacent evidence, non-done stage, and open/blocked finding rows in this file; it runs no build or Runtime work and is not a second completion authority, evidence database, or source-wide staleness system.

Keep `assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md` in the same dependency order as this guide; if the template order is wrong, correct and validate the template before using or releasing that Skill version — never work around a misordered template by executing later sections first.

## Round discipline

For every validation round:

1. Run every safely reachable check in the current stage.
2. Record the complete finding inventory in the TODO with `open` or `resolved` state and concrete evidence.
3. Group findings by shared root cause and module.
4. Repair the complete batch.
5. Re-run affected focused checks, then only the stage checks invalidated by the repair.
6. Repeat until no open finding remains.

Stop early only when continuation is impossible, risks data loss or security, corrupts protected state, or invalidates the remaining results. A recoverable failure is not a reason to stop the round.

## Semantic execution contract and canary

Before model authoring, close one semantic execution row for every acceptance journey in the existing backend PRD; reference those rows from the session TODO instead of creating a second plan. Each row binds:

- the requirement and actor to a project-provisioned Runtime identity and formal session/principal source;
- every Runtime-owned context fact or canonical identifier to the typed client, formal seed/admin path, or persisted Runtime response that supplies it;
- fresh setup identities/records and any explicit dependency on another journey;
- the command surface and the actor-visible read surface;
- a positive oracle naming the target identity and required non-empty facts;
- the exact denial, concealment, validation, or conflict status/error category plus unchanged-state oracle;
- the durable database effect, replay/restart requirement, and authoritative reconciliation source.

Runtime-owned identities, hierarchy values, paths, claims, cursors, and fingerprints are opaque values. Carry the formal returned value unchanged across metadata, seed data, Handler inputs, persisted records, and acceptance. Do not synthesize them from display names or conventions, and do not trim, append, case-fold, or otherwise normalize them unless the published Runtime contract explicitly owns that transformation. A missing formal source is a blocking Foundation/Runtime gap, not permission to inject a request claim or guess a representation.

For each scope-sensitive row, prepare one target record and probe it through real sessions with otherwise equivalent requests: the matching actor observes that exact record and a non-empty expected result; the non-matching actor receives the contractually specified concealment/denial and produces no durable effect; when a broader application role is in scope, it observes the same record. A success status with an empty collection, null result, zero aggregate, or wrong target is a failure unless the confirmed requirement calls for that exact value. A negative probe passes only on its intended stable status/error category and unchanged state, never on an arbitrary `4xx`, `not found`, or setup failure.

Choose one highest-risk row as the semantic canary, favoring a journey that crosses the most of identity/context resolution, data scope, project Action, multi-record persistence, actor-visible projection, and restart/replay. After the full model is applied, source is finalized, and focused tests pass, execute that row before the broad Runtime integration round. If it fails, mark every dependent journey blocked by that root cause, finish the reachable failure inventory, repair the owner once, and rerun the canary plus only invalidated checks. Do not spend a full acceptance round rediscovering the same upstream mismatch, but never use the canary to shrink the complete model or final denominator.

### Produce the backend dependency PRD

For a new project or a complete frontend Mock-to-Runtime replacement, create or update `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` from `assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md`. This is not a marketing PRD or a pixel inventory: it is the accepted demand contract for what Runtime and project metadata/source must provide. For a light existing-project increment, record an equivalent traceable PRD delta in the current session TODO or update the accepted backend PRD, and reference the unchanged baseline.

**Reference mode for structured input.** A source is structured when its rules live in stable titled/numbered sections citable as `<doc> §N`. Test per requirement: if one section states the rule completely, cite it — do not restate it; rewrite only what must be assembled from scattered evidence (Mock adapters, tests, verbal decisions, multiple documents). A reference-mode PRD carries requirement IDs, classifications, owner/capability mapping, decisions, acceptance criteria, and the matrices, each row citing its source section; restating an already-structured source is prohibited waste. Both modes keep the Resolve-critical-ambiguity table and full traceability.

Read frontend evidence in this order: route/page registry and user journeys; typed application API; Mock adapters/fixtures; state stores and hooks; form/list/detail/report components; permission/menu guards; tests and stories; visible copy. Also read the current explicit requirement and latest accepted product/design documents. Legacy APIs or prior backends are `legacy_reference` until the current requirement or frontend confirms them.

This inspection is read-only even when later integration is authorized to repair frontend source. A Mock fixture, adapter behavior, test expectation, or visible affordance proves demand or a current assumption; it does not establish a business rule without higher-precedence evidence.

Use this precedence when evidence conflicts:

1. explicit current user decision;
2. latest accepted requirement or design contract;
3. latest implemented frontend behavior;
4. typed API and Mock semantics;
5. frontend tests;
6. legacy/reference implementation.

Do not erase conflicts using precedence alone. Record the conflict, affected requirement IDs, selected authority, and confirmation evidence. Classify every item as `confirmed`, `recommended`, `open`, `frontend_only`, or `legacy_reference`.

Extract at least:

- pages, routes, entry conditions, actors, journeys, and observable success;
- canonical object identities, fields, relations, list/detail/form/report shapes, filters, search, sort, and pagination;
- commands, outcomes, bulk operations, state transitions, approvals, cancellation/correction paths, and durable side effects;
- roles, permissions, record scope, sensitive fields, menu visibility, and allow/deny behavior;
- validation, stable errors, conflicts, optimistic concurrency, transaction boundaries, idempotency, and replay behavior;
- calculations with inputs, units, formula, policy/version date, rounding point/mode, examples, and refund/correction behavior;
- schedulers, automations, notifications, connectors, files, audit, outbox, and external effects;
- presentation-only behavior that remains `frontend_only` and must not create backend metadata.

Build a traceability matrix with one row per requirement: `frontend evidence → requirement ID → Runtime owner/capability → model resource or approved source gap → permission/data scope → acceptance journey`. Where the frontend exposes a typed API, count its backend-bound operations and account for every one in the matrix as implemented, platform-reused, frontend-only, superseded, or open. Every route must map to a journey or an explicit frontend-only disposition. Every write operation must name authorization, validation/error behavior, transaction boundary, idempotency/retry policy, durable result, and acceptance proof.

Matrix and contract-table cells are phrases, not sentences. Once a fact is in a table (or cited by section), do not restate it in prose; prose is only for what no table column captures.

### Resolve critical ambiguity

Do not infer any unresolved object identity, financial or payroll formula, permission boundary, state transition, inventory effect, or external side effect. Keep the affected requirement and downstream modeling items blocked until the user or accepted requirement evidence confirms the rule. A visual button, fixture value, label, or legacy endpoint proves demand exists but does not prove the business rule.

Non-critical open items may proceed only when the PRD records the assumption, decision owner, fallback, and excluded acceptance scope. Never mark them `confirmed` merely because implementation is possible.
